fields.title: Spinal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Spinal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the spine requires highly accurate diagnosis and carefully chosen comprehensive treatment. Israeli medical centres give patients access to the latest advances in medical science and practice, together with a high standard of medical care.

Diagnosis of spinal cancer

  1. Doctors carry out a medical examination and take a history in order to understand the patient's symptoms and the course of the illness, and then set out a plan of action.
  2. Laboratory tests, including a full blood count and other specialised tests that help identify the cancer.
  3. This is followed by imaging using high-resolution 3 Tesla MRI.
  4. PET-CT provides detailed images of the tumour and allows its metabolic activity to be assessed.
  5. Biopsy — needed for definitive confirmation of the diagnosis and to establish the type of tumour. (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatments for spinal cancer

  1. Minimally invasive, low-trauma surgery, which allows the tumour to be removed with minimal risk and few complications.
  2. Next, radiotherapy and stereotactic radiosurgery are used to deliver high doses of radiation precisely to the tumour.
  3. Chemotherapy is used to destroy cancer cells, particularly where the cancer has spread.
  4. Hormone therapy and endoscopic techniques also add to the range of treatments, offering gentler approaches.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of spinal cancer

  • First, advanced medical equipment and highly qualified specialists deliver effective diagnosis and treatment.
  • Second, an individual approach to treatment guarantees a personalised treatment plan for every patient, which is extremely important in this condition.
  • Finally, comprehensive rehabilitation helps patients recover after treatment and return to a full life.

Choosing Israel for the treatment of spinal cancer gives access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists — and, most importantly, attentive support at every stage of treatment and rehabilitation.

fields.title: Prostate cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Prostate cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Prostate cancer is one of the most significant cancers in men, particularly in the over-50 age group. Israel offers advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment, combining the latest scientific advances with an individual approach to every patient. All of this helps achieve the best possible quality of life after treatment.

Diagnosis of prostate cancer

  1. Digital rectal examination (DRE)
    allows the prostate to be assessed for hardening or other abnormalities.
  2. Laboratory tests:
    — PSA blood test (prostate-specific antigen): The main marker for screening and monitoring prostate cancer. A raised PSA level may indicate the presence of cancer, although it can also rise in other conditions of the prostate.
    — Full blood count: Includes checking haemoglobin, white cells and other important indicators that may reveal inflammation or other abnormal changes in the body.
    — Blood biochemistry: Assessment of the functioning of the kidneys, liver and other organs is important in deciding whether certain treatments, including chemotherapy, are possible.
  3. Prostate biopsy
    under ultrasound guidance — an accurate method of confirming a diagnosis of prostate cancer
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. Prostate MRI: A highly accurate imaging method that helps establish the exact position of the tumour.
  5. PSMA PET
    (positron emission tomography with prostate-specific membrane antigen) is an innovative imaging method that considerably improves diagnostic accuracy, allowing even microscopic metastases to be detected.

Treatments for prostate cancer

  1. Active surveillance
    is recommended in low-risk prostate cancer with no signs of spread.
  2. Surgery
    carried out using robotic systems — the da Vinci robot — for minimally invasive removal of the prostate.
  3. Radiotherapy and brachytherapy
    are used to destroy cancer cells with minimal damage to the surrounding tissue.
  4. HIFU (high-intensity focused ultrasound)
    a method using high-intensity focused ultrasound to destroy cancer cells locally.
  5. Tookad therapy
    an innovative approach using a combination of a photosensitising agent and laser irradiation to destroy cancer cells.
  6. NanoKnife
    an advanced technology for targeted treatment of the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of prostate cancer

Israeli clinics are known for their achievements in oncology. Patients are offered a comprehensive approach, from accurate diagnosis using PSMA PET through to individualised treatment programmes that may include both traditional and innovative methods. The high qualifications of Israeli specialists, modern equipment and attention to patients' quality of life after treatment make Israel a preferred destination for the treatment of prostate cancer at international level.

fields.title: Rectal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Rectal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the rectum is one of the more common cancers. It requires a comprehensive approach to diagnosis and treatment. Israeli medical centres use innovative methods of treatment and diagnosis, offering patients effective treatment programmes aimed at a full recovery or at extending life and quality of life as far as possible.

Diagnosis of rectal cancer

  1. Colonoscopy
    is the main diagnostic method, allowing a tumour to be detected and a biopsy taken for histological analysis.
  2. Laboratory tests: full blood count, biochemistry, and tests for tumour markers including carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and Ca19.9, which help assess the activity of the disease and monitor the response to treatment.
  3. Sigmoidoscopy
    makes it possible to see the inner surface of the lower part of the rectum and detect abnormalities.
  4. PET
    is used to assess the stage of the disease, detect metastases and judge the effectiveness of treatment. It gives full information about how far the cancer has spread.
  5. Biopsy
    is the key step in confirming the presence of cancer cells and establishing the type of tumour
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).

Treatments for rectal cancer

  1. Surgery
    remains the main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour and the affected sections of bowel.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy cancer cells, particularly after an operation, to reduce the risk of recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy
    is often used before surgery to shrink the tumour and afterwards to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    are newer approaches to treatment, directed at particular molecular targets and at activating the patient's immune system to fight the cancer.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of rectal cancer

  • Advanced technology and highly qualified specialists deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to design treatment that best matches their needs and the features of their illness.
  • Value for money makes treatment in Israel accessible to many patients looking for quality medical care at a competitive price.

Israeli clinics offer the most effective and safe treatments for rectal cancer, combining the latest medical developments with care for every patient and aiming for the greatest possible improvement in their health and quality of life.

fields.title: Cervical cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Cervical cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cervical cancer is one of the most serious cancers in women. Israeli medical centres offer an advanced approach to treating this disease, with the emphasis on innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment that help not only fight the disease effectively but also preserve patients' fertility, which is particularly important for young women.

Diagnosis of cervical cancer

  1. Medical examination and history
    are the first step in diagnosis, allowing specialists to assess general health and identify possible symptoms.
  2. Colposcopy makes it possible to examine the cervix in detail under high magnification in order to identify abnormalities.
  3. Laboratory tests
    include blood tests for tumour markers, which may indicate the presence of cancer cells in the body.
  4. PET-CT is used to assess how far the disease has spread, detect metastases and help plan treatment.
  5. Biopsy provides cervical tissue for detailed examination under the microscope, which is the definitive confirmation of the diagnosis
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).

Treatments for cervical cancer

  1. Surgery
    may range from conisation of the cervix to hysterectomy. It all depends on the stage of the disease and the patient's plans for having children.
  2. Radiotherapy
    is used on its own or in combination with surgery, and is aimed at destroying the cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    is used in advanced cancer to destroy cancer cells throughout the body.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    offer new possibilities in the treatment of cervical cancer, directed at particular biological targets in the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of cervical cancer

  • Advanced equipment and highly qualified specialists
    deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient
    makes it possible to develop the best treatment plan, taking account of every aspect of the illness and her personal preferences.
  • Value for money
    makes Israel an attractive choice for many patients looking for quality medical care at an affordable price.
  • Particular attention to preserving fertility
    reflects the aim of preserving patients' quality of life after treatment as fully as possible.

Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to the treatment of cervical cancer, combining the newest medical developments with deep care for the wellbeing of every patient.
